definition: Adaptable means capable of adjusting to new conditions.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word adaptable. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know adaptable should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The pothos is a famously adaptable houseplant, growing just as happily in a dim hallway as on a bright windowsill.
Flexible is weaker than adaptable, a flexible person will bend when plans change, while an adaptable person actively reshapes how they work to fit the new situation.
Protean is stronger than adaptable, an adaptable colleague adjusts to change, while a protean one seems to transform completely for every new role.

Versatile means useful or skilled in many different roles — a versatile player covers several positions. Adaptable is about adjusting rather than multiplying uses: an adaptable tool may do one job while retuning itself to conditions. Versatile counts the roles; adaptable describes the adjusting.

Malleable means easily shaped or reshaped by an outside force, the way warm metal takes whatever form the hammer gives it. An adaptable person or design does the adjusting itself, actively reshaping how it works to fit new conditions. Malleable things are changed by others; adaptable things change themselves.

Adjustable means built with settings someone can change by hand — an adjustable wrench, an adjustable desk. The change comes from whoever turns the dial. Adaptable goes further: an adaptable system or person responds to new conditions on its own, without waiting to be reset.

Adaptable means capable of adjusting to new conditions.
Marisol, the softball team's utility player, is prized for being adaptable: in a single weekend tournament she played shortstop, catcher, and left field.
Each position demands different skills and instincts, and Marisol adjusts to whichever one the team needs from game to game.
Adjusting successfully to changing demands is exactly what adaptable means.
Common in everyday and workplace English, often in the pattern adaptable to, as in adaptable to change.
Watch the spelling trap with adoptable, which differs by one letter but means suitable to be adopted, as with a shelter pet.

Biologists once assumed the city would starve its wildlife; the coyote proved them wrong.
Tracked across Chicago, the animals turned out to be remarkably adaptable, remaking their own habits to fit whatever block they landed in.
Suburban coyotes hunted at dawn; downtown ones went fully nocturnal, learned traffic patterns, and raised pups in a parking-garage drainage ditch.
No one trained them, and nothing about their bodies changed — the shift happened in behavior, animal by animal.
The species did not merely endure new conditions; it changed its own ways to meet them, season after season.
